rationale: This is a mechanical recombination of two archived signals ("Debt-Funded Overexpansion Distress" and "Accrual-Covered Debt Raise") that simply drops the shared lct/act leg, and its two conditioning terms are themselves the well-published asset-growth and accrual anomalies, so little incremental information is likely.

The conditioning block is byte-identical to the archived "Preferred Payout Debt Overhang" and only the financing leg is changed from level to first difference — a cosmetic level-to-delta variant that will also be very noisy since dvt−dvc is lumpy and mostly zero.

This is a near-mirror of the archived "Distressed Dividend Restoration" (same dividend leg and same −re/at term, with only the Δoancf sign flipped), so it largely re-tests the negative of information already measured rather than adding an independent mechanism.

The ex-post "did the raise repair the balance sheet" framing is a genuinely different design from the archive's contemporaneous issuance-times-distress signals, though −Δre is close to a plain low-profitability proxy and the equity-issuance leg overlaps the known net-issuance anomaly.

Sequencing the repurchase ahead of the liquidity deterioration is a defensible reframing of the weak "Levered Buyback Cash Drain" family, but part of the conditioning (falling cash after a buyback) is partly mechanical and the incremental novelty over archived buyback-strain signals is modest.

The financing leg (debt raised net of the contemporaneous change in cash) is a genuinely new construct that isolates borrowing immediately consumed rather than banked, and it is internally consistent with the stated negative sign; the only caveat is that the term also fires on pure cash drawdowns with little issuance.
